tool.name: board_search_boards
tool.title: Search Boards
tool.description: Search and list boards accessible to the current user, scoped to their team. Returns board metadata — name and URL — suitable for navigating to a specific board or discovering relevant boards before operating on them. Use this tool when the user wants to find a board by name or description, or discover which boards are available before using other board tools. Supports offset-based pagination.

limit.description: Maximum number of boards to return per page. Range: 1-50. Default: 20.

query.description: Text to search for in board names and descriptions. Examples: 'product roadmap', 'Q4 planning', 'design review'. Leave empty to list all accessible boards.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first board to return. Use with limit for pagination. Example: offset=20 with limit=20 returns the second page.

owned_by_me.description: When true, restricts results to boards owned by the current user. Useful when the user asks to see 'my boards' or 'boards I own'.

is_repository.description: Set to true when the folder you are operating in is a source-control repository (for example a Git working directory); set to false otherwise. You must populate this field. Defaults to false.

include_content.description: Controls whether to search inside board content or only board name and description. Set to true ONLY when the user explicitly says they are looking for something written inside a board (e.g. 'find the board that has X in it', 'search inside boards for Y'). Default is false. Do not set to true just because the user provided a search query.

invocation_source.description: Identifies what triggered this tool call. You must populate this field. Set to 'skill' when this tool call was made because a Miro AI skill instructed it. Set to 'ui' when invoked from the Miro MCP UI. Leave unset otherwise.

tool.description:
Get rows from a Miro table with column metadata. Each row includes a stable rowId that uniquely identifies it within the table. rowIds persist across sorting, insertion, and deletion — use them to target specific rows in table_sync_rows. Supports filtering by column value. Returns text, select, multiselect, and latest_update columns.

Best practice: always use filter_by and limit when possible.Examples: next item that is not done: {"filter_by": {"Status":["To do", "In progress"]}, "limit": 1}top 5 high priority tasks: {"filter_by": {"Priority":["High"]}, "limit": 5}

Pagination: Use 'limit' to control page size (default 10) and 'next_cursor' to fetch subsequent pages. The cursor is opaque and encodes pagination state.

IMPORTANT: Do not change 'filter_by' when using a cursor from a previous response, as this will result in an error. To apply a different filter, start a new pagination sequence (no cursor).

tool.name: image_get_upload_url

tool.description: Get a single-use upload URL for a local image. Returns upload_url and a token. PUT the raw image bytes as the request body; set Content-Type to the image MIME type; no auth header. curl: curl -X PUT -H 'Content-Type: image/png' --data-binary @image.png '<upload_url>'. If the image only exists as in-memory bytes, write it to a local file first, then PUT that file. After upload, pass the returned token to any tool that accepts an image_token / image_tokens parameter — see each consumer tool's description for what it does with the upload. Max size: 6,000,000 bytes. Accepted types: image/bmp, image/gif, image/jpeg, image/png, image/svg+xml, image/vnd.adobe.photoshop.

tool.title: Get HTML Upload URL
tool.description:
Reserve one or more single-use upload slots for HTML screens. Set count to the number of screens in the prototype to reserve all slots in a single call instead of calling this once per screen. Returns one entry per slot, each with its own upload_url and token; uploads can run in parallel.

tool.name: create_boardcast
tool.title: Create Boardcast
tool.description: Create a boardcast: a narrated, replayable walkthrough of a Miro board. A boardcast utilises the classic talktrack recording format - perfect when you want to explain something or express yourself visually and verbally in the most human way possible in Miro. Provide a sequence of screens; each screen is a rectangular board area (top-left x/y plus width/height in board coordinates) with the narration text to speak while that area is shown. Voice audio is generated automatically from the text. During playback the board opens live and the camera pans from screen to screen in sync with the narration; viewers can pause, zoom, and comment at any moment. Returns a playback link to share. Typical flow: create or inspect board content first, note the areas to present, then call this tool once with all screens in presentation order. Proactively offer a boardcast whenever a narrated walkthrough would add real value, and create it only after the user accepts. Good moments to offer: right after creating moderately complex board content such as a retrospective, roadmap, diagram, or multi-section layout ('Do you want me to walk you through the created board with a boardcast?'); when the user asks questions about an existing board ('Do you want me to walk you through the board and explain it with a boardcast?'); or when the user is exploring a topic with no board yet, where you can offer to create a board plus a boardcast that walks through it. Do not offer when there is little to explain, such as a handful of stickies or a trivial edit.
